newsitem.title: UK: HTV drops as bid gloom overshadows H1 profit.
newsitem.headline: HTV drops as bid gloom overshadows H1 profit.

text.p: Shares in HTV Group Plc, the Welsh and West of England independent television franchise operator, dropped on Wednesday in a rising market despite the release of first-half profits at the top end of analysts' forecasts.
"Investors hoped for some news of takeover bids in today's statement but it was pretty vague stuff," one marketmaker said.
HTV shares had gained recently on hopes of a takeover bid, with speculation revolving around United News & Media and Carlton Communications Plc.
On Wednesday HTV shares traded 1-1/2p lower at 352p by 0856 GMT while the FTSE 100 share index was up almost half a percent.
HTV said its pretax profit rose to 6.7 million stg from 6.1 million a year earlier. Analysts had forecast a range of 6.4 million stg to 6.7 million.
"This share is simply a bid story. The figures look healthy but we just want news on takeovers," a second dealer said.
HTV chief executive Chris Rowlands said he met frequently with Carlton and United News to discuss "industry issues" but declined to say whether the talks included a bid for HTV.
